analysis.summary: Kubernetes v1.38.0-alpha.1 是一个早期预发布版本，主要聚焦于清理已毕业的特性门控、修复多个关键Bug、增强调度器稳定性与安全性，并移除部分已废弃的API。
key_changes: 移除 PodSchedulingReadiness 特性门控，该功能已永久启用 - [PR #141741](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141741)
移除 SeparateTaintEvictionController 特性门控，污点驱逐现在由独立控制器永久处理 - [PR #141789](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141789)
外部调度器插件（Out-of-tree kube-scheduler plugins）的 NominatedPodsForNode 方法签名变更，需添加 logger 参数 - [PR #142118](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142118)
移除已废弃的 metrics.k8s.io/v1alpha1 API - [PR #140862](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140862)
移除已废弃的 apidiscovery.k8s.io/v2beta1 API 及相关特性门控 - [PR #141208](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141208)
移除已锁定GA的特性门控 CustomResourceFieldSelectors 和 CRDValidationRatcheting - [PR #141207](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141207)
调度器支持在 Topology-Aware Scheduling (TAS) 中尊重 NominatedNodeName - [PR #139472](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139472)
为 CompositePodGroup 的 MinGroupCount 字段添加可变性支持，允许动态调整 - [PR #141023](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141023)
important_bugfixes: 修复调度器预抢占时，使用过滤器扩展器（filter extenders）导致的错误 - [PR #135486](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135486) - **影响：** 使用调度器扩展器的集群，预抢占可能失败，影响高优先级Pod的调度

修复设备管理器（Device Manager）在重建 allocatedDevices 时可能丢失进行中（in-flight）的设备预留，导致同一设备被分配给多个Pod - [PR #137534](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137534) - **影响：** 使用GPU、FPGA等扩展资源的集群可能出现设备分配冲突，导致Pod启动失败或设备访问错误
修复调度队列中因竞争条件导致Pod被永久忽略的Bug - [PR #139450](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139450) - **影响：** 极少数情况下，Pod可能卡在调度队列中无法被调度，且无错误日志

修复 CPUManager 在跨NUMA节点分配独占CPU时，错误地缩小了 TopologyManager 提供的NUMA亲和性范围 - [PR #139456](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139456) - **影响：** 配置了 `distribute-cpus-across-numa: "true"` 和 `prefer-closest-numa-nodes: "true"` 的节点，可能无法获得最优的NUMA亲和性，影响性能敏感型工作负载

修复 PersistentVolume 指标 `pv_collector_total_pv_count` 对所有CSI卷错误地报告插件名称为 `N/A` - [PR #139356](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139356) - **影响：** 基于此指标的监控和告警（如 `kube_persistentvolume_plugin_type_counts`）会丢失CSI卷的准确分类信息
修复 NodeRestriction 准入插件在解析Pod的CSI卷源失败时，未正确回退检查授权，导致特定情况下节点服务账户令牌请求被错误拒绝 - [PR #140607](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140607) - **影响：** 当集群中存在未找到的CSIDriver、PVC或PV时，节点的令牌请求可能失败
修复 code-generator 生成的客户端会覆盖用户传入的 config.NegotiatedSerializer - [PR #140317](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140317) - **影响：** 依赖自定义 NegotiatedSerializer 的客户端（如为了保留未知字段）将无法正常工作
security_issues: 修复 kube-scheduler 在日志级别 `-v=2` 时，将调度器扩展器配置中的TLS私钥（keyData）以base64形式记录到日志中 - [PR #140519](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140519) - **风险级别：** 中 - 仅影响配置了扩展器TLS内联证书且开启`-v=2`日志的场景
修复 kubelet 在启动时，将 `--manifest-url-header` 配置的头部值（如Authorization令牌）以明文记录到日志中 - [PR #140220](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140220) - **风险级别：** 中 - 影响使用静态Pod URL并配置了认证头部的kubelet
修复 kubectl debug 的 sysadmin 配置文件，使其能感知Windows节点并应用正确的Host Process Container配置，而非Linux特权模式 - [PR #138182](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138182) - **风险级别：** 低 - 增强了Windows节点调试的安全性
performance_improvements: 调度器队列指标现在支持 CompositePodGroup - [PR #141800](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141800) - **提升：** 为基于CompositePodGroup的工作负载调度提供了可观测性
API Server 为聚合的 OpenAPI v2 端点 (`/openapi/v2`) 添加请求指标 - [PR #140888](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140888) - **提升：** 完善了API Server的监控覆盖
将 `volume_operation_errors_total` 指标从Alpha升级到Beta稳定性 - [PR #141536](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141536) - **提升：** 增强了存储操作错误监控的可靠性
breaking_changes: 外部调度器插件必须更新：`NominatedPodsForNode` 方法的第一个参数现在必须是 `logger klog.Logger` - [PR #142118](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142118) - **影响：** 所有实现此接口的自定义调度器插件需要重新编译并适配新签名，否则升级后会导致调度器崩溃
移除 metrics.k8s.io/v1alpha1 API - [PR #140862](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140862) - **影响：** 任何直接调用此API版本的客户端或工具将失效，应迁移至 metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1
移除 apidiscovery.k8s.io/v2beta1 API 及 AggregatedDiscoveryRemoveBetaType 特性门控 - [PR #141208](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141208) - **影响：** 依赖此API版本的客户端代码需要更新导入路径和类型到 v2

废弃并重命名指标 `endpoint_slice_controller_changes` 为 `endpoint_slice_controller_changes_total` - [PR #140447](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140447) - **影响：** 监控仪表板和告警规则如果使用了旧指标名，需要更新。新版本中两个指标同时存在，旧指标已被标记为废弃

修复 Quantity 类型中负值舍入逻辑和超大DecimalSI值字符串表示的Bug，可能改变序列化/反序列化行为 - [PR #138510](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138510), [PR #140459](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140459) - **影响：** 极少数处理极端数值边界或依赖特定字符串表示格式的应用程序可能观察到行为变化
recommendations: **对于生产环境：** 此版本为Alpha，**绝对不应用于生产**。仅用于早期集成测试和评估变更影响。

**升级前检查清单：** 1) 检查是否使用自定义的、实现了 `NominatedPodsForNode` 的调度器插件，并准备更新。2) 从 kube-controller-manager 的 `--feature-gates` 中移除 `SeparateTaintEvictionController`（如果显式设置过）。3) 审查代码和工具是否依赖已被移除的 `metrics.k8s.io/v1alpha1` 或 `apidiscovery.k8s.io/v2beta1` API。
**测试重点：** 在测试集群中，重点验证：1) 调度器扩展器（extender）在预抢占场景下的功能。2) 设备（如GPU）的分配是否正常，无冲突。3) 使用了 `distribute-cpus-across-numa` 和 `prefer-closest-numa-nodes` 的工作负载性能。4) 所有涉及 `resource.Quantity` 类型处理的边缘用例。
**监控与日志：** 升级测试环境后，检查调度器、kubelet日志中是否还有敏感信息泄露。更新监控仪表板，将 `endpoint_slice_controller_changes` 指标引用替换为 `endpoint_slice_controller_changes_total`。
analysis.risk_assessment: 整体风险评估：**中高**（对于Alpha版本而言属正常范围）。此版本包含多项破坏性API变更和关键Bug修复，对调度器、设备管理、资源计算等核心子系统有实质性改动。虽然修复了许多严重问题，但新引入的变更本身需要充分测试。建议的升级时机：仅限具备完整回滚方案的开发或集成测试环境。需要特别关注的方面包括：自定义调度器插件的兼容性、扩展资源管理、以及任何对已移除API的隐性依赖。

141741.title: Remove PodSchedulingReadiness feature gate
141741.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/sig scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Removes the `PodSchedulingReadiness` feature gate from Kubernetes. The feature graduated to GA and was locked to default in v1.30, and has completed the required version emulation deprecation window.

- Removed `PodSchedulingReadiness` from `pkg/features/kube_features.go`.
- Regenerated compatibility lifecycle feature lists (`test/compatibility_lifecycle/reference/versioned_feature_list.yaml` and `feature_list.md`).
- Verified all unit and integration tests pass.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3521

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
action required: Removed the `PodSchedulingReadiness` feature gate from `kube-scheduler` and related components as the feature is permanently enabled.
```

- [KEP]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/3521-pod-scheduling-readiness

141789.title: Remove SeparateTaintEvictionController feature gate
141789.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup
/sig scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Removes the `SeparateTaintEvictionController` feature gate from Kubernetes. The feature gate graduated to GA in v1.34 and has completed the required 3-release version emulation deprecation window.

This PR:
- Removes `SeparateTaintEvictionController` feature gate from `pkg/features/kube_features.go`.
- Removes required feature gate check on `newTaintEvictionControllerDescriptor` in `cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/core.go`.
- Removes legacy embedded taint manager in `NodeLifecycleController` (`pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go`).
- Updates unit tests in `cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/controllermanager_test.go` to test standalone taint eviction controller directly without feature gating.
- Cleans up integration tests in `test/integration/node/lifecycle_test.go`.
- Updates compatibility lifecycle reference documentation (`versioned_feature_list.yaml` and `feature_list.md`).

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3902

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
AI was used in preparing and verifying this change. The author carefully reviewed the code before submitting the PR.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
action required: Removed the `SeparateTaintEvictionController` feature gate from `kube-controller-manager`. Remove this gate from existing `--feature-gates` configuration before upgrading. Taint-based eviction is now permanently implemented by the standalone taint eviction controller, which can still be disabled using `--controllers=-taint-eviction-controller`.
```

142118.title: Use HandleErrorWithLogger instead of HandleError in workload_forest
142118.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup
#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Propagates contextual `logger klog.Logger` to `PodNominator.NominatedPodsForNode` and `ctx context.Context`  to `SchedulingQueue.GetPod`.

This allows queue and nomination lookup operations to forward contextual loggers to internal helpers and error handlers (`utilruntime.HandleErrorWithLogger`). This solves the TODO we had in [`workload_forest.go`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/83619fca3eed26f9f7cba894d74c00ddb79dfded/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/workload_forest.go#L136-L137)
#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
N/A
#### Special notes for your reviewer:
1. **`SchedulingQueue.GetPod(ctx context.Context, ...)`**: Updated to accept `context.Context` instead of `klog.Logger`. Since `GetPod` is primarily called from unit and integration tests where `ctx` is already present, passing `ctx` directly avoids wrapping every call with `klog.FromContext(ctx)` and keeps future `ctx` propagation open without tripping `logcheck`. Internally, `GetPod` extracts the logger via `klog.FromContext(ctx)` to call the private `getPod` helper.
2. **`PodNominator.NominatedPodsForNode(logger klog.Logger, ...)`**: Kept `klog.Logger` here so the entire `PodNominator` interface remains consistent (`AddNominatedPod`, `DeleteNominatedPodIfExists`, `UpdateNominatedPod`, and `NominatedPodsForNode` all take `logger klog.Logger`).
#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Action required: Out-of-tree kube-scheduler plugins using the `NominatedPodsForNode` method must now pass `logger klog.Logger` as the first argument.
```
#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:
```docs
```
#### AI usage disclosure:
YES - AI pair programming assistant  was used to update method signatures, propagate logger parameters across test suites, and verify integration tests.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Currently, when the scheduler is configured with a filter extender and that extender rejects a Pod, the DefaultPreemption plugin throws an error because it finds no pod need to be evicted for the pod to schedule.

This happens due to a mismatch during the preemption phase: while evaluating potential victims on a node (SelectVictimsOnNode), the default preemption logic runs only the built-in filter plugins but skips the filter extenders. As a result, it incorrectly assumes that the pod can always be scheduled, which conflict with the filter result so it throw an error.

This PR addresses the problem by assume this situation as expected and continue to call processPreemption() which assign the preempt extender to find victims.

139472.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Makes Topology-Aware Workload Scheduling (TAS) respect `NominatedNodeName` (NNN) when picking a placement for a PodGroup. Today TAS ranks placements by score and a random tiebreak, ignoring NNN, so a gang nominated to specific nodes can land elsewhere. Pod-by-pod scheduling already tries the nominated node first; this closes the gap at the placement level.

The core scheduler now evaluates the placement matching the pods' NNN before any other. If the gang is feasible there, it uses that placement and skips the rest. Otherwise it falls back to the normal score-based selection across all placements.

- Short-circuit only when the gang is feasible on the nominated placement now, not via preemption. If it isn't, the nominated placement competes with the rest under normal scoring, so NNN never schedules fewer pods.
- When nominations span more than one placement, no single placement clearly matches, so we skip the shortcut and fall back to normal scoring. This keeps the result independent of the order plugins hand us placements.
- Test plumbing: steps framework gained `UpdatePodStatus` and a `WaitForPodsNominated` barrier so the integration test sets NNN before the gang's cycle without racing.

140674.title: [Quantity] Add resource.MaxMilliQuantity and fix the Quantity docs
140674.body:
Replaces #140636. I force-pushed a broken commit to that branch (an amend on a shallow clone, which produced a parentless commit carrying the whole tree), and GitHub closed it on the spot and will not reopen a branch that has been force-pushed since. Same branch, same work. Sorry for the noise, @pohly.

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind cleanup
/sig api-machinery

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`MaxMilliValue` and the `MilliValue` / `ScaledValue` doc comments tell you to compare `Quantity.Value()` against `MaxMilliValue` to check whether `MilliValue()` is safe to call:

```go
// The maximum value we can represent milli-units for.
// Compare with the return value of Quantity.Value() to
// see if it's safe to use Quantity.MilliValue().
MaxMilliValue = int64(((1 << 63) - 1) / 1000)
```

That check is unreliable, as you noted on #140161: `Value()` projects through int64, so it overflows for a quantity larger than int64 and reports a huge quantity as small enough. A parsed `18446744073709551616` has a `Value()` of `0`, which is `<= MaxMilliValue`, so the recommended check passes for 2^64.

This adds `MaxMilliQuantity()` and points the docs at `Quantity.Cmp`, which compares directly instead of projecting through int64 and so stays correct above the int64 range:

```go
if q.Sign() >= 0 && q.Cmp(resource.MaxMilliQuantity()) <= 0 {
    // q.MilliValue() will not overflow
}
```
`Sign()` is exact, so this is a complete check for a possibly-negative `q`; the bound alone is one-sided (a large negative `q` sorts below it but its milli value is below MinInt64).

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Follow-up from your review on #140161 (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140161#discussion_r3594007620). No separate issue filed.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

- **`MaxMilliQuantity` is `NewMilliQuantity(mostPositive, DecimalSI)`, not `MaxMilliValue` as a Quantity.** `MaxMilliValue` is `MaxInt64 / 1000` under integer division, so it floors the real bound to a whole number, and a quantity may be fractional: `9223372036854775807m` has a `MilliValue()` of exactly `MaxInt64` and is safe, but sorts above `MaxMilliValue`. Returning the floored value would have made the doc's "largest" false by 0.807, so the helper returns the actual bound. The test pins that: at the bound `MilliValue()` is `MaxInt64` exactly, and `9223372036854775807m` is inside the bound with a `MilliValue()` of `MaxInt64` too, which the floored version would have excluded.
- **`MinMilliQuantity` is not here, and that is the interesting part.** You asked for it on r3601187240. I wrote it, then found that its guard cannot hold today: `Value`/`MilliValue`/`ScaledValue` do not round negatives as documented once a quantity is Dec-backed, so a quantity inside the bounds can still come back wrong. `MustParse("-9.5Gi").Value()` returns `+8246196746`, which also defeats the `quantity.Value() < 0` check in `validateBasicResource` (`pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go:7952`). That is #110653, open since 2022 and confirmed by @yliaog, with a fix already up in #138510. I would rather not ship a helper whose stated purpose is negative-side safety while the negative side is broken, so I left it out and will add it once #138510 lands. I have reviewed that PR and verified it makes the guard sound.
- **Three claims in the `Quantity` type doc did not hold**, all corrected here. It said no quantity may exceed 2^63-1 in magnitude and that a larger number is capped, that a quantity carries at most three decimal places and more precision is rounded up, and its `decimalSI` grammar left out `n` and `u`. Measured: the cap is real but it belongs to **parsing**, and only for binarySI (`8Ei` is 2^63 and parses as 2^63-1, silently; arithmetic sails past it, `4Ei` + `4Ei` is `8Ei`), a decimal `18446744073709551616` keeps its value, `1.2345` keeps its precision (`String` reports it as `1234500u`), and `suffix.go` does list `n` and `u`. The rounding the old text described is real too, but it happens at parse, away from zero, and at nano rather than milli, which is why its example (`0.1m` becoming `1m`) is wrong: `0.1m` stays `100u`, and it is `MilliValue()` that reads 1.
- **Rendering.** The serialization grammar sat in Markdown fences, which `go doc` does not understand: it prints the fences literally and reflows every production into one run-together paragraph. Two bullet lists used column-0 dashes, which `go doc` merges into a single paragraph. Both are reformatted to what `go doc` renders, matching the `CanonicalizeBytes` doc in the same file. No wording changed for that part.
- **The `ceil` / "away from 0" contradiction is left alone on purpose.** `Value` documents away from zero, `MilliValue` and `ScaledValue` document `ceil`, and those disagree for a negative q. I had them aligned here and backed it out: picking the winner decides the contract, that is #110653's job, and #138510 is already up with the code change. This PR only adds the overflow advice to those two comments.
- **The docs do not promise a specific overflowed result.** The Dec path ends in `big.Int.Int64()`, which Go documents as undefined out of range, so the doc says the result is unusable rather than naming a value, and no test asserts one.
- **Function, not a `var`.** `Quantity` is a mutable struct with pointer-receiver mutators, so an exported `var` could be scribbled on by any caller. The call site `q.Cmp(MaxMilliQuantity())` reads the same as the existing `maxRatio.Cmp(*resource.NewQuantity(1, resource.DecimalSI))` in `pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go`.
- **On deprecating `MaxMilliValue`:** you floated it. I left it in place and reworded its doc to say what it actually bounds (a whole number, not a quantity). A `// Deprecated:` tag would raise SA1019 for every downstream that vendors apimachinery, and it is still a correct bound for an integer. Happy to add the deprecation as a follow-up if you want callers pushed off it.
- **No call sites converted.** The in-tree `Value()`/`MaxMilliValue` sites are `plugin/pkg/admission/limitranger/admission.go:300` and `:375`, and `pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go:7761`. All three read a quantity that is not sign-validated, so converting them is a behaviour change rather than a cleanup, and worth its own PR. Happy to do it if you would rather see the helper exercised here.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**

```release-note
Added resource.MaxMilliQuantity(), which returns the largest quantity whose MilliValue and ScaledValue(resource.Milli) do not overflow an int64. For a non-negative quantity, compare it against the returned bound with Quantity.Cmp before calling MilliValue or ScaledValue(resource.Milli). Comparing Quantity.Value against resource.MaxMilliValue for this is unreliable, because Value itself overflows for a quantity larger than int64.
```

138510.title: [Quantity] Fix scaledValue to round negative Quantity values away from zero
138510.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`resource.Quantity.Value()` and `MilliValue()` are documented to round *"to the nearest integer away from zero,"* but small negative values were rounding toward positive infinity. `ParseQuantity("-.484785E-7466").Value()` returned `+1` instead of `-1`.

The bug is in `scaledValue` in `staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/scale_int.go`, which has two scale-down paths; both were wrong for negative inputs:

**int64 fast path.** Go's integer division truncates toward zero and `mod` takes the sign of the dividend. The old code added `1` whenever `mod != 0`, so `-1500 / 1000` returned `-1` instead of `-2`. Now a positive `mod` adds `1` and a negative `mod` subtracts `1`, moving the result further from zero in both cases.

The fast-path guard was also a single signed comparison, `unscaled.Cmp(maxInt64) < 0`, which holds for every negative value however large, so negatives at or below `math.MinInt64` reached `unscaled.Int64()` out of range. The guard now also requires `unscaled.Cmp(minInt64) > 0`, so those values fall through to the big.Int path.

**big.Int path.** `big.Int.DivMod` is Euclidean: the remainder is always in `[0, divisor)`. For a negative dividend the quotient is already floored, which *is* the away-from-zero direction for negatives, so no adjustment is needed. The old code incremented unconditionally; now only the positive-dividend case with a non-zero remainder gets the `+1`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #110653

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Behavior change is strictly from wrong-direction rounding to the documented direction for negative values:

| Input | Old `Value()` | New `Value()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-.484785E-7466` | `1` | `-1` |
| `-1500m` | `-1` | `-2` |
| `-0.0005` | `1` | `-1` |

Positive values are unaffected (same `+1` when remainder is non-zero, same no-op when zero). Exact multiples are unaffected in both signs.

Coverage:

139356.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The metric `pv_collector_total_pv_count` (which feeds the `kube_persistentvolume_plugin_type_counts` recording rule) reports `plugin_name="N/A"` for all CSI-provisioned PersistentVolumes instead of the correct `kubernetes.io/csi:<driver>` value.

**Root cause:** Commit 9e29f95618c ("Refactor controller-manager volume plugins") replaced `ProbeControllerVolumePlugins` with `ProbeProvisionableRecyclableVolumePlugins` for the PV binder controller. The CSI plugin (`kubernetes.io/csi`) implements none of these interfaces — it delegates all operations to external CSI drivers — so it was silently dropped from `volumePluginMgr`.

`metrics.Register` was still passed `&ctrl.volumePluginMgr`, so at metric collection time `getPVPluginName()` called `pluginMgr.FindPluginBySpec()` for each PV. For any CSI PV, this returned `ErrNoPluginMatched`, causing the code to fall back to the `pluginNameNotAvailable` sentinel (`"N/A"`).

**Fix:** Initialize a dedicated `metricsPluginMgr` from `ProbePersistentVolumePlugins` (which returns all plugins with no filter, including CSI) and pass that to `metrics.Register` instead of `volumePluginMgr`. The operational `volumePluginMgr` (used for provisioning/recycling) is unchanged.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The offending commit is 9e29f95618c. Before that change, the old `ProbeControllerVolumePlugins` included the CSI plugin unconditionally, so `volumePluginMgr` could resolve CSI PVs. The refactor correctly narrowed `volumePluginMgr` for operational purposes but inadvertently broke metric collection, which needs a broader plugin set.

The fix intentionally keeps `volumePluginMgr` narrow (provisionable/deletable/recyclable only) and introduces a separate `metricsPluginMgr` to avoid any unintended side effects on the provisioning/recycling paths.

139450.title: scheduler: call Done before requeueing pod in AddUnschedulablePodIfNotPresent
139450.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`AddUnschedulablePodIfNotPresent` defers `Done()` to the end of the function, but the broadcast that wakes waiting `Pop` callers fires before that deferred call. On a multi-CPU system a `Pop` goroutine can acquire `aq.lock` in the window between the broadcast and the deferred `Done()`, find the pod UID still present in `inFlightPods`, and have `unlockedMoveEntityToInFlight` silently discard it — causing the pod to vanish from the scheduling queue permanently with no error logged.

140459.title: Fix Quantity.String() dropping the suffix for DecimalSI values above 10^18
140459.body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`resource.Quantity.String()` silently drops the magnitude for `DecimalSI` quantities whose canonical base-10 exponent exceeds `10^18`, corrupting the value and breaking the `String()`/JSON round-trip invariant.

`CanonicalizeBytes` discarded the `ok` return value of `constructBytes`:

```go
suffix, _ := quantitySuffixer.constructBytes(10, exponent, format)
return number, suffix
```

The `DecimalSI` suffix table only defines suffixes up to `E` (`10^18`). For a larger canonical exponent, `constructBytes` returns `(nil, false)`, but because `ok` is ignored an empty suffix is appended and the exponent is lost:

```
resource.MustParse("1000E").String()   // "1"      (should be 1e21)
resource.MustParse("5000E").String()   // "5"      (should be 5e21)
resource.MustParse("1000000E").String()// "1"      (should be 1e24)
```

The value is stored faithfully (`AsDec()` returns the true `10^21`, and `Cmp`/`Add` operate on the true magnitude), so it passes validation and is only corrupted at serialization — it then round-trips through `String()`, `MarshalJSON()`, `ToUnstructured()`, JSON and YAML to a number `10^21` smaller, with no error. `DecimalExponent` is unaffected (it already renders `1e21` correctly). `BinarySI` is capped only at *parse* time (to `MaxInt64`); arithmetic is not capped, so a `BinarySI` quantity can grow past `Ei` (2^60) and hit the same missing-suffix path. This PR fixes that branch too — a value past `Ei` (e.g. 2^70) now falls back to decimal exponent notation instead of dropping the suffix (which serialized it to `1`).

This PR keeps the `ok` result and falls back to decimal exponent notation (`e`) when no `DecimalSI` suffix exists, preserving the magnitude:

```
resource.MustParse("1000E").String()   // "1e21"
resource.MustParse("5000E").String()   // "5e21"
resource.MustParse("1000000E").String()// "1e24"
```

Values that already have a suffix (`1E`, `999E`, `100E`, …) are unchanged. Added `TestQuantityString` cases covering exponents at and above `10^18`, including the re-parse (round-trip) and negative-value checks already performed by that test.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

None.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

An alternative would be to cap `DecimalSI` at parse time (as `BinarySI` is), matching the godoc note that over-large numbers "will be capped". That is a lossy, larger behavior change; this PR takes the minimal, non-lossy path of restoring the `String()` round-trip invariant without changing what values can be parsed or stored. Happy to switch approaches if preferred.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**

```release-note
Fixed `resource.Quantity.String()` (and `MarshalJSON`/`ToUnstructured`) silently dropping the magnitude for `DecimalSI` quantities larger than 10^18 (for example `1000E`), and for `BinarySI` quantities grown past `Ei` via arithmetic (for example 2^70), which corrupted the value and broke round-tripping through String/JSON/YAML. Such quantities now serialize to an exact base-10 representation: decimal exponent notation where trailing zeros allow it (for example `1e21`), otherwise the full decimal integer (for example 2^70 becomes `1180591620717411303424`).
```

```
echo '{"securityContext":{"windowsOptions":{"runAsUserName":"NT AUTHORITY\\NetworkService"}}}' > custom.json
```

`BenchmarkDropManagedFields` encodes an exemplar Pod (3 field managers) and LISTs of 1000 the way the apiserver does (protobuf with its pooled allocator). Changes are for drop versus full, n=6, p≤0.004:

| Object | Format | CPU | Bytes written | B/op |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pod | JSON | −23% | −36% | +71% ¹ |
| Pod | Protobuf | +8% ¹ | −50% | +381% ¹ |
| Pod | CBOR | −82% | −34% | −93% |
| PodList | JSON | −24% | −36% | −2% |
| PodList | Protobuf | −3% | −50% | ~ |
| PodList | CBOR | −82% | −34% | −93% |
| Unstructured | JSON | −43% | −36% | −32% |
| Unstructured | CBOR | −43% | −34% | −24% |
| UnstructuredList | JSON | −40% | −36% | +277% ² |
| UnstructuredList | CBOR | −44% | −34% | −24% |

¹ The single-object spine copy: 1.25 KiB and ~0.4 µs, which is most of what a pooled protobuf encode allocates. End to end, including the client's decode, a JSON GET allocates 1.7 KiB more and is 4–8% faster; a protobuf GET allocates 5–10% less and is 0–2% faster.
² Per-item map clones, so objects shared with the watch cache aren't mutated. Real CR LISTs deep-copy during conversion anyway; with that step the drop is −43%.

CBOR gains the most because full encoding converts `FieldsV1` from JSON on every encode.

```
go test ./pkg/endpoints/handlers/ -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkDropManagedFields$' -count 6 > drop.txt
```

#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

like all other core Kubernetes binaries. This eliminates the glibc version

instead, which resolves through NSS either way.

Kubelet now builds as a static binary (CGO_ENABLED=0). 139270.title: kube-scheduler: RunFilterPluginsWithNominatedPods bypasses Scheduler Extenders during preemption.
139270.body:
### What happened?

When the kube-scheduler evaluates preemption victims, it relies on RunFilterPluginsWithNominatedPods (in pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go) to verify if removing lower-priority pods will make enough room on a node.

Currently, this function only evaluates in-tree Framework Plugins (f.RunFilterPlugins). It completely bypasses registered Scheduler Extenders. Because Extenders are never queried during this preemption dry-run, the scheduler incorrectly assumes no pods need to be evicted, and preemption completely fails for resources managed by Extenders.


[https://github.com/Project-HAMi/HAMi/issues/1494#issuecomment-3574678309](HAMi issue 1449)
[https://github.com/Project-HAMi/HAMi/issues/1878](HAMi issue 1878).

### What did you expect to happen?

If RunFilterPlugins returns a success during the nominated pods loop, the scheduler should also query f.extenders before officially concluding that the high-priority pod fits on the node.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Register a Scheduler Extender that manages a constrained custom resource (e.g., the HAMi project for vGPU slicing).
2. 
3. Deploy a low-priority pod that consumes all available Extender resources on a node.
4. 
5. Deploy a high-priority pod requesting those same Extender resources.
6.

139186.title: Pod can become ignored by the scheduling queue when unlikely timing happens
139186.body:
### What happened?

When pod is re-added to the scheduling queue after a failed binding cycle, the queue's Pop can be passively waiting for any pod to be added to the activeQ (and backoffQ when SchedulerPopFromBackoffQ is enabled). When an unlikely timing happens, the pod can be popped from the scheduling queue after its re-added ([here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/661b086ee0d115150cb222694b44b103c88a3a5d/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L887)), but before the `Done` is called for this pod ([here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/661b086ee0d115150cb222694b44b103c88a3a5d/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L845)). In such case, the pod is dropped from the scheduling queue completely:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/661b086ee0d115150cb222694b44b103c88a3a5d/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/active_queue.go#L267-L269

/sig scheduling

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod should not be dropped, but scheduled.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Add a `time.Sleep(time.Second)` after this line to make the failure occur each attempt:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/661b086ee0d115150cb222694b44b103c88a3a5d/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L891

Then, execute the test:
```go
func TestPopIgnoringPod(t *testing.T) {
	logger, ctx := ktesting.NewTestContext(t)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()

	pod := st.MakePod().Name("pod1").UID("pod1").Obj()
	q := NewTestQueueWithObjects(ctx, newDefaultQueueSort(), []runtime.Object{pod})
	q.Add(ctx, pod)

	// Simulate failed attempt that makes the pod unschedulable.
	poppedPod := popPod(t, logger, q, pod)
	poppedPod.UnschedulablePlugins = sets.New("fooPlugin1")

	// Activate the pod, meaning when it's re-added to the scheduling queue, it will skip unschedulable
	q.Activate(logger, map[string]*v1.Pod{pod.Name: pod})

	poppedPodCh := make(chan *framework.QueuedPodInfo)
	go func() {
		poppedPodCh <- popPod(t, logger, q, pod)
	}()
	time.Sleep(time.Second)

	if err := q.AddUnschedulableIfNotPresent(logger, poppedPod, q.SchedulingCycle()); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("Unexpected error from AddUnschedulableIfNotPresent: %v", err)
	}
	select {
	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
		t.Errorf("Pop timed out")
	case pod := <-poppedPodCh:
		t.Logf("Got pod: %v", pod.Pod.Name)
	}
}
```

  ```yaml
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: "176"
      nvidia.com/gpu: "8"
    limits:
      cpu: "176"
      nvidia.com/gpu: "8"
  ```

  TopologyManager selects an all-NUMA affinity because the pod requests 8 GPUs distributed across all 4 NUMA nodes:

  ```text
  Best TopologyHint bestHint={"NUMANodeAffinity":15,"Preferred":false}
  Topology Affinity affinity={"NUMANodeAffinity":15,"Preferred":false}
  ```

  CPUManager receives this affinity:

  ```text
  AllocateCPUs numCPUs=176 socket="1111"
  ```

  However, the final CPU allocation only uses 3 NUMA nodes:

  ```text
  AllocateCPUs result="32-61,64-93,96-124,160-188,192-220,224-252"
  ```

  So CPUManager appears to treat the TopologyManager affinity as an allowed NUMA set, then reselects the minimum number of NUMA nodes needed to satisfy the CPU request.

  On this node, 176 CPUs can fit into 3 NUMA nodes, so the final CPUSet is distributed roughly as:

  ```text
  59 + 59 + 58
  ```

  This is not aligned with the GPU/NIC topology selected by TopologyManager.

### What did you expect to happen?

  When TopologyManager selects a multi-NUMA affinity and passes it to CPUManager, CPUManager should preserve that topology intent when allocating exclusive CPUs.

  In this case, since the 8 GPUs and NICs span all 4 NUMA nodes, we expected the exclusive CPU allocation to also cover all 4 NUMA nodes, roughly:

  ```text
  44 + 44 + 44 + 44
  ```

  At minimum, there should be an opt-in CPUManager static policy option to distribute exclusive CPUs across all NUMA nodes in the TopologyManager affinity, instead of shrinking the allocation back to the
  minimum number of NUMA nodes required by the CPU request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

 1. Use a node with this topology:

  ```text
  256 logical CPUs
  4 NUMA nodes
  8 GPUs distributed across all 4 NUMA nodes
  ```

  2. Configure kubelet with static CPUManager and NUMA distribution:

  ```yaml
  cpuManagerPolicy: static
  cpuManagerPolicyOptions:
    distribute-cpus-across-numa: "true"

  topologyManagerPolicy: best-effort
  topologyManagerPolicyOptions:
    prefer-closest-numa-nodes: "true"
  ```

  3. Create a Guaranteed pod requesting 8 GPUs and 176 exclusive CPUs:

  ```yaml
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: "176"
      nvidia.com/gpu: "8"
    limits:
      cpu: "176"
      nvidia.com/gpu: "8"
  ```

  4. Check kubelet logs for TopologyManager and CPUManager allocation:

  ```console
  journalctl -u kubelet | grep -E "TopologyHints generated|Best TopologyHint|Topology Affinity|AllocateCPUs"
  ```

  5. Observe that TopologyManager selects the all-NUMA affinity, but CPUManager allocates the final CPUSet from only 3 NUMA nodes.

### Anything else we need to know?

 This looks related to CPU/device NUMA alignment discussed in #122295, but it is different from the `align-by-socket` behavior addressed by #136572.

  In this case:

  - `align-by-socket` is not enabled
  - TopologyManager already passes the all-NUMA affinity to CPUManager
  - the issue happens later, when CPUManager allocates CPUs and shrinks the final CPUSet to fewer NUMA nodes

  A possible direction is to add a new opt-in CPUManager static policy option, for example:

  ```text
  distribute-cpus-across-topology-affinity=true
  ```

  or:

  ```text
  distribute-cpus-across-affinity=true
  ```

  Intended behavior:

  > When TopologyManager provides a multi-NUMA affinity to CPUManager, CPUManager distributes exclusive CPUs across all NUMA nodes in that affinity, instead of shrinking the allocation back to the minimum
  number of NUMA nodes required by the CPU request.

  This should likely be opt-in, not a default behavior change, because existing users may rely on CPUManager minimizing the number of NUMA nodes used.

  Open questions:

  - For `best-effort` TopologyManager policy, should CPUManager strictly fail if it cannot allocate within the selected affinity, or should it fall back to the existing allocation behavior?
  - Should this behavior apply to non-preferred hints selected by `best-effort`, or only to preferred hints?
  - Should this option require `distribute-cpus-across-numa=true`?
  - How should this interact with `align-by-socket`?

140132.title: kubelet logs --manifest-url-header credentials (Authorization / API keys) to runtime logs
140132.body:
### What happened?

When kubelet is configured with `--manifest-url` and credential-bearing `--manifest-url-header` values (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer …` or `X-API-Key: …`), those header values are written to kubelet runtime logs at startup, in cleartext.

At static-pod source init, `makePodSourceConfig` copies the config map into a plain `http.Header` and logs it directly:

```go
// pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go:372-393
manifestURLHeader := make(http.Header)
if len(kubeCfg.StaticPodURLHeader) > 0 {
    for k, v := range kubeCfg.StaticPodURLHeader {
        for i := range v {
            manifestURLHeader.Add(k, v[i])          // values copied into a plain http.Header
        }
    }
}
...
if kubeCfg.StaticPodURL != "" {
    logger.Info("Adding pod URL with HTTP header", "URL", kubeCfg.StaticPodURL, "header", manifestURLHeader)  // <-- sink
    config.NewSourceURL(logger, kubeCfg.StaticPodURL, manifestURLHeader, ...)
}
```

The codebase already knows this field is secret and masks it elsewhere:

```go
// pkg/kubelet/apis/config/types.go:107
StaticPodURLHeader map[string][]string `datapolicy:"token"`
```

…and the *config-dump* path redacts it before logging the full `KubeletConfiguration` (`cmd/kubelet/app/server.go:287-290` masks the map to `<masked>`). But `makePodSourceConfig` logs the **runtime `http.Header` copy**, not the config map — so neither the `datapolicy:"token"` tag nor the logging-mask applies, and the header values ship out verbatim. (`datapolicy` only fires on a strongly-typed field argument; here the value has been flattened into an `http.Header` passed as a generic `"header"` argument.)

### What did you expect to happen?

`makePodSourceConfig` should not log the header values. The `datapolicy:"token"` tag and the `server.go:287-290` config-mask both express the intent that `StaticPodURLHeader` is secret; this code path bypasses both by logging a runtime copy. The sink should mask/drop the `header` field (e.g. log only that headers are present, or redact like the config-dump path does). Redaction must not depend on operators avoiding sensitive headers, since the field is the documented place to put upstream auth.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Copy-paste into a shell **inside the kubernetes repo** (auto-detects root). It drops a same-package Go test under `pkg/kubelet` that calls the real `makePodSourceConfig` with a custom `logr` sink capturing klog output, sets `Authorization: Bearer static-pod-url-secret`, and asserts the secret appears in the captured logs. Cleans up after itself; no cluster or running kubelet needed.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
F="$ROOT/pkg/kubelet/zz_poc_staticpodheader_logleak_test.go"
trap 'rm -f "$F"' EXIT
cat >"$F" <<'GOEOF'
package kubelet

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/go-logr/logr"
	metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
	kubeletconfiginternal "k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/apis/config"
	kubeletutil "k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/util"
	"k8s.io/klog/v2"
)

type pocSink struct{ buf *bytes.Buffer }

func (s *pocSink) Init(logr.RuntimeInfo)          {}
func (s *pocSink) Enabled(int) bool               { return true }
func (s *pocSink) Info(_ int, msg string, kv ...interface{}) {
	fmt.Fprintln(s.buf, append([]interface{}{msg}, kv...)...)
}
func (s *pocSink) Error(err error, msg string, kv ...interface{}) {
	fmt.Fprintln(s.buf, append([]interface{}{msg, err}, kv...)...)
}
func (s *pocSink) WithValues(kv ...interface{}) logr.LogSink { return s }
func (s *pocSink) WithName(string) logr.LogSink              { return s }

func TestPOCStaticPodURLHeaderLogLeak(t *testing.T) {
	var logs bytes.Buffer
	ctx := klog.NewContext(context.Background(), logr.New(&pocSink{buf: &logs}))

	const secret = "Bearer static-pod-url-secret"
	kubeCfg := &kubeletconfiginternal.KubeletConfiguration{
		StaticPodURL:        "http://127.0.0.1:1/static-pods.yaml",
		StaticPodURLHeader:  map[string][]string{"Authorization": {secret}},
		HTTPCheckFrequency:  metav1.Duration{Duration: time.Hour},
	}
	deps := &Dependencies{PodStartupLatencyTracker: kubeletutil.NewPodStartupLatencyTracker()}

	if _, err := makePodSourceConfig(ctx, kubeCfg, deps, "node-a", func() bool { return true }); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("makePodSourceConfig: %v", err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(logs.String(), secret) {
		t.Fatalf("secret NOT in logs:\n%s", logs.String())
	}
	t.Logf("VULNERABLE: static pod URL header secret written to kubelet logs\n%s", logs.String())
}
GOEOF
( cd "$ROOT" && go test ./pkg/kubelet -run TestPOCStaticPodURLHeaderLogLeak -count=1 -v 2>&1 | grep -E 'VULNERABLE|Adding pod URL|PASS|FAIL|ok ' )
```

Expected: printed lines show the secret in the kubelet log output, then `PASS`:

```text
VULNERABLE: static pod URL header secret written to kubelet logs
    Adding pod URL with HTTP header URL http://127.0.0.1:1/static-pods.yaml header map[Authorization:[Bearer static-pod-url-secret]]
--- PASS: TestPOCStaticPodURLHeaderLogLeak (0.00s)
ok  	k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet
```

i.e. the `Authorization: Bearer static-pod-url-secret` value is logged verbatim by `Adding pod URL with HTTP header`.

### Anything else we need to know?

- This is secret disclosure of upstream-manifest credentials to kubelet logs, at default verbosity. It is a duplicate of the same finding already recorded internally as `kubelet_staticpodurlheader_log_leak`.
- Distinct from `kubelet_configz_staticpodurlheader_leak` (the `/configz` JSON path, different sink and code path) — both leak the same `StaticPodURLHeader` field but via different endpoints; both capitalize on the fact that `makePodSourceConfig`/`setConfigz` bypass the `datapolicy`/config-mask that `server.go:287-290` applies.
- Affects kubelet configured with `--manifest-url` + `--manifest-url-header`. Nodes using only `--pod-manifest-path` are not affected.

140096.title: kube-scheduler logs extender TLS private key (keyData) at -v=2
140096.body:
### What happened?

`kube-scheduler` writes the full resolved `KubeSchedulerConfiguration` to its startup log at verbosity `-v=2`. If any extender is configured with inline TLS credentials (`tlsConfig.keyData`), the **PEM client private key is emitted as base64** in that log line.

Sink — `cmd/kube-scheduler/app/options/configfile.go:94`:

```go
if loggerV.Enabled() {
    loggerV.Info("Using component config", "config", buf.String()) // buf = YAML of full config
}
```

`buf.String()` is produced by the v1 YAML encoder. The v1 `ExtenderTLSConfig.KeyData` (`staging/src/k8s.io/kube-scheduler/config/v1/types.go:399`) is `[]byte json:"keyData"` with **no redaction and no `datapolicy` tag**, so the encoder base64-encodes the raw key bytes into the YAML string. The internal type *does* tag the field `datapolicy:"security-key"` (`pkg/scheduler/apis/config/types.go:340`), but that tag only works on a strongly-typed klog argument — here the key is already flattened into one YAML string passed as a single `"config"` string, so the datapolicy filter never fires.

### What did you expect to happen?

The private key should never appear in logs. The `datapolicy:"security-key"` tag on `KeyData` expresses that intent explicitly; this code path silently bypasses it because the whole config is serialized to a YAML string before logging. Either the sink should redact `keyData`/`certData`/`caData` before logging, or `LogOrWriteConfig` should not log secrets-bearing sections at `-v=2`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Copy-paste into a shell **inside the kubernetes repo** (auto-detects repo root). It drops an inline Go test that calls the real `LogOrWriteConfig` with `-v=2`, captures klog output, and prints the leaked key. Cleans up after itself; no cluster needed.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
DIR="$ROOT/cmd/kube-scheduler/app/options"
F="$DIR/zz_poc_keydata_leak_test.go"
trap 'rm -f "$F"' EXIT
cat >"$F" <<'GOEOF'
package options

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/base64"
	"flag"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
	"k8s.io/klog/v2"
	"k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/apis/config"
	configv1 "k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/v1"
)

func TestPOCKeyDataLeak(t *testing.T) {
	state := klog.CaptureState()
	t.Cleanup(state.Restore)
	var fs flag.FlagSet
	klog.InitFlags(&fs)
	_ = fs.Set("v", "2")
	_ = fs.Set("logtostderr", "false")
	_ = fs.Set("alsologtostderr", "false")
	var out bytes.Buffer
	klog.SetOutput(&out)

	pem := []byte("-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nATTACKER_RECOVERABLE_EXTENDER_KEY\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----")
	cfg := &config.KubeSchedulerConfiguration{
		TypeMeta:  metav1.TypeMeta{APIVersion: configv1.SchemeGroupVersion.String(), Kind: "KubeSchedulerConfiguration"},
		Extenders: []config.Extender{{URLPrefix: "https://extender.internal", EnableHTTPS: true, TLSConfig: &config.ExtenderTLSConfig{KeyData: pem}}},
	}
	if err := LogOrWriteConfig(klog.Background(), "", cfg, nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	klog.Flush()

	logged := out.String()
	enc := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(pem)
	if !strings.Contains(logged, enc) {
		t.Fatalf("private key NOT in logs:\n%s", logged)
	}
	t.Logf("scheduler log contains keyData:\n%s", logged)
}
GOEOF
go test ./cmd/kube-scheduler/app/options -run TestPOCKeyDataLeak -count=1 -v
```

Expected: test **passes**, and the `scheduler log contains keyData` output shows a `tlsConfig:` block with `keyData: <base64>` that `base64 -d` decodes back to `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----…`.

### Anything else we need to know?

- Production call site: `cmd/kube-scheduler/app/server.go:477` (`Setup` → `LogOrWriteConfig`), reached on every scheduler start.
- `certData` and `caData` (also `[]byte`) are logged the same way; `keyData` is the secret.
- This is secret disclosure in logs. Per the template's note, this may warrant **private disclosure** via https://kubernetes.io/security rather than a public issue — flagging so maintainers can route it.
